name: Hold the Pendle PT instead of the token when its implied rate clears the token's own interest by 5%
thesis: Where YT buyers pay for points, the PT trades well above the interest the token itself pays. A holder who switches from the token into its PT keeps the same credit and gives up the points. Chosen on markets maturing before 2025-09-01 and tested on trades entered after it, the switch made +7.09% a year over the token's realised floating (t 7.11, 1,004 trades, 96% positive). It is +7.83% TVL-weighted, +4.35% at $1M a trade, +5.55% with an earlier cutoff, and +7.48% after charging the reward tokens the holder would also have collected. The book carries only the markets whose token pays measured interest ($6.6M of the $10.0M that qualifies today): for a token that pays nothing, "over floating" is the whole implied rate, and that comparison is the dollar-PT-against-the-savings-rate family, which lost out of sample after defaults.
mechanism: YT = SY - PT, so every dollar YT buyers pay for points or for leverage on the floating rate is a dollar off the PT. The PT holder is short the token's points and long its fixed rate; the premium is the market price of the points. In points markets the PT trades a median 4.28% over trailing interest, against 1.78% elsewhere. The out-of-sample excess rises with the spread at entry (+2.97% at >=0, +7.09% at >=5%, +12.31% at >=12%), so the premium was not competed away inside the test window.
legs: exit (or do not buy) the yield token
buy its PT through the Pendle AMM at the size that maximises dollars a year through the pool
hold to expiry and redeem; re-enter the next market that clears the 5% rule
kill_criteria: matured switches under the 5% rule realise less than +2% a year over the tokens' floating across a trailing 90 days
live capacity under the rule below $2M
any single protocol above 30% of the live book
median implied minus trailing interest in points markets below 2%
risks: the excess is the price of the points the holder gives up; if the airdrop is worth more, holding the token was better, and nothing here measures airdrops
the token's credit is unchanged: dollar PTs on sUSDX, RLP, YU and msUSD returned 1 to 33 cents in the same history, so this is a switch for holders, not a dollar yield

10 of today's 18 qualifying markets are tokens that pay no measured interest (AUSD, USDat, apxUSD, Axis USDx, Royco junior); for them the edge is the whole implied rate, and against the savings rate after defaults the dollar version lost out of sample
impact is AMM-only (limit-order depth not read); selling a PT before expiry crosses the same curve

regime: part of the excess is that floating rates fell over the holding periods of 2025-26, which a fixed rate locks against; the no-points markets also show it (+9.6% pooled per capital-year out of sample, coordinator recomputation from trades.json.gz), so it is a forward-rate premium as much as a points price, and a rising-rate year would shrink it

evidence.notes: research/2026-10-09/pendle_history/findings.md; analysis.json results.b_pt_when_implied_over_trailing (chosen spread>=500bp) and live_books; robustness in analysis_size1m.json and analysis_cut20250401.json; scripts/pendle_history.py with 38 tests

quotes.note: 8 live markets whose token pays measured interest clear implied - trailing-7d >= 5%: $6.6M at each pool’s dollar-maximising size earns $216k a year over the tokens’ own floating (10 more markets, $3.4M, are tokens paying no interest and are excluded). Out of sample the rule made +7.09% a year (mark-to-market book); recomputed from trades.json.gz, +8.4% pooled per capital-year before reward tokens, 96% of 1,004 trades positive.
